verdict.rationale: Auth0 core docs describe exactly this: registering your own API as an OAuth 2.0 resource server (auth0-docs-2), issuing tokens to third-party/M2M clients via Client Credentials flow (auth0-docs-8, auth0-docs-25, auth0-docs-54), and general access-management docs note scopes work 'whether it's for first-party apps, third-party integrations, or Machine-to-Machine communications' (auth0-docs-81, auth0-docs-56). This is Auth0's standard authorization-server role. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of third-party developer onboarding/dynamic client registration workflow and independent hands-on corroboration of building a public OAuth provider on Auth0 (evidence is vendor docs only).
